isolated rain showers or localized thunderstorms according to the Philippine Atmospheric Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration PAGASA In its 5 a m regional weather forecast issued on elsewhere in Mindanao during severe thunderstorms The forecast is valid from 5 a m on October 20 until 5 a m on October 21 covering the island's major regions including the Zamboanga Peninsula Northern Mindanao Davao Region SOCCSKSARGEN Caraga and the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao BARMM Zamboanga Peninsula faces persistent rain and thunderstorm activity Zamboanga City peninsula's localities are expected to range from the mid 20s to the low 30s Celsius with daytime highs reaching 34 C in Zamboanga City Zamboanga del Norte and Isabela City Zamboanga Sibugay is forecast to record temperatures of 24 C to 32 C while Zamboanga del Sur may experience temperatures ranging from 26 C to 34 C PAGASA's warning highlights the potential for flash floods and landslides particularly in areas where rainfall becomes moderate to heavy Communities near rivers and creeks in low-lying areas and along or below steep slopes should remain alert to rapidly changing conditions The ITCZ is a zone where winds converge encouraging the development of clouds and rain-producing weather systems Its influence can sustain periods of rainfall and thunderstorms although the timing and text: As communities continue to recover from widespread flooding caused by the southwest monsoon habagat Senator Christopher Bong Go urged the Department of Public Works and Highways DPWH to expedite the construction and completion of permanent evacuation centers nationwide Heavy monsoon rains recently inundated several areas across Luzon with provinces such as Pampanga among the severely affected areas prompting government rescue operations in Central Luzon During the Senate deliberations on the DPWH's proposed 2027 budget on September 25 Go emphasized that recurring flooding highlights the urgent need for safe and dedicated evacuation shelters instead of temporary facilities such as schools and gyms Ako mismo pinupuntahan ko talaga yan Pampanga Bulacan naaawa talaga ako sa Pilipino Go said recalling the difficult conditions he personally witnessed in submerged communities Tulungan n'yo naman po sila Kayo po ang nandiyan sa executive department pakiuna na lang po na ma-address itong problema ng flooding po Kawawa talaga At yung iba po naiiwan sa mga evacuation centers Yung iba eskwelahan gym Hindi sila kumportable yung iba walang maayos na sanitation he added Go serves as the principal author and co-sponsor of Republic Act No 12076 or the Ligtas Pinoy Centers Act which was enacted in December 2024 and mandates the establishment of evacuation centers in every city and municipality Addressing DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon Go urged the agency to prioritize the construction of these facilities amid the country's frequent experience of typhoons earthquakes and seasonal flooding Sana po mabigyan n'yo po ito ng prayoridad itong mga evacuation centers Mapapakinabangan po ito ng mga kababayan natin Batas na po ito Go asserted He also called on the DPWH to review existing projects funded under the 2025 and 2026 budgets to ensure that near-complete structures are completed without further delay In response Secretary Dizon reported that 464 of the 492 Ligtas Pinoy evacuation center projects had been completed as of late August while 24 remained under construction He added that approximately PHP 3.06 billion had been programmed for 2027 for the construction of two evacuation centers per region We will prioritize Mr Chairman You have our assurance po Dizon assured the Senate panel Mr Malasakit Bisyo Ang Mag Serbisyo Senator Bong Go

text: DAVAO FLOODING AND THE DUTERTES A Balanced Assessment AN HONEST STARTING POINT Flooding in Davao is a legitimate concern that deserves serious attention Some of the criticisms are grounded in real events including a genuine solid-waste crisis that cost lives this year At the same time much of the social-media commentary exaggerates the problem blurs who's actually responsible and paints this as a uniquely Duterte-family failure A fair assessment holds both things at once real gaps and a national context that critics conveniently leave out NATIONAL REALITY CHECK Flood control is a hard problem everywhere in the Philippines Outdated drainage garbage-choked waterways siltation and urbanization that outpaced 1970s-era infrastructure overwhelm every major city in heavy rain No LGU not Manila not Cebu not Davao has a flood-free rainy season Anyone claiming otherwise about any city is selling something Davao carries the same systemic pressures as its peers but has put more visible work into the problem than most WHAT HAS BEEN DELIVERED Multiple drainage and flood-control projects since 2022 prioritized in high-risk districts including river rehabilitation on the Matina Bunawan and Davao River systems Seven DPWH pumping stations already operating across the city Jerome Mamay Agdao Marginal-to-Magsaysay Ponce Roxas ext Mabini ext plus two more in Laverna with a third proposed City-funded drainage rehabilitation including PHP 35 million for the CSC road drainage and PHP 40 million for the Kabacan creek in Ecoland Residents in upgraded zones report noticeably faster water recession after heavy downpours compared to before these projects this is anecdotal rather than a published city metric but it's a consistent report worth taking seriously rather than dismissing Rodrigo Duterte's earlier line-item vetoes of questionable DPWH insertions reflected a genuine stance against pork-barrel-style spending which matters when we're talking about whether flood money gets spent honestly These are real verifiable steps not just promises WHERE THE RECORD IS GENUINELY WEAK AND NEEDS TO BE SAID PLAINLY This is the part critics will hammer so let's not soften it on May 20 2026 a portion of the New Carmen sanitary landfill collapsed after days of heavy rain killing at least one person and leaving others missing on top of injuries and displaced families DENR suspended the landfill days later cited multiple violations of the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act and permanently closed the old site in June That is not a maintenance footnote it was a fatal disaster and it happened on this administration's watch Pretending otherwise would be dishonest BEYOND THAT INCIDENT THE UNDERLYING PROBLEMS ARE REAL AND LONGSTANDING The landfill was already operating well past design capacity for years before it collapsed waste disposal roughly doubled from 2010 levels by 2025 and this was a known documented problem not a surprise Drainage systems in several barangays have not received consistent desilting Uncollected and improperly dumped garbage continues to clog canals and drainage inlets citywide and enforcement against illegal dumping and drainage encroachment remains inconsistent The new landfill and expansion projects were already underway before the collapse which shows the problem was recognized but recognizing a problem is not the same as having fixed it in time Full transparency on the landfill collapse investigation and a public accounting of why the old site was allowed to run so far past capacity is the least residents deserve COMPARATIVE PERSPECTIVE None of this erases the comparison that matters how does Davao stack up against LGUs facing the same pressures On project delivery and the resources actually put toward flood mitigation pumping stations river rehabilitation drainage funding Davao has more to point to than many cities of similar size and budget That doesn't make Davao's flooding acceptable It means the uniquely incompetent Duterte fiefdom narrative pushed on social media doesn't survive contact with what other LGUs are or aren't doing with comparable resources KEY CLARIFICATIONS The PHP 51 billion figure widely cited for Rep Paolo Duterte's district 2020-2022 is routinely presented online as if it were all flood-control spending It wasn't DPWH-Davao itself has clarified the figure later refined to PHP 49.8 billion covered the district's entire infrastructure portfolio roads bridges multipurpose buildings and major projects like the Davao Coastal Road and Bypass Road DPWH's own breakdown puts the flood-control share at roughly PHP 9 billion a fraction of the total Treating the full PHP 51B as a flood-control budget then pointing at continued flooding as proof the money didn't work is a category error not an accountability finding That said a real question remains open and shouldn't be waved away

text: Super Typhoon Champi locally named Rosal has entered the Philippine Area of Responsibility PAR This remains an extremely powerful storm with sustained winds of 250 km/h 155 mph and a central pressure of 922 hPa Satellite imagery shows a well-organized super typhoon with excellent outflow allowing it to maintain its intensity WHAT ABOUT THE PHILIPPINES The good news is that Champi is forecast to remain well northeast of mainland Luzon A direct landfall in the Philippines is not expected However that does not mean there will be no impacts According to the PAGASA advisory discussed in this update Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No 1 has been issued for parts of Batanes the Babuyan Islands Cagayan and Isabela This indicates winds of 39-61 km/h are possible within 36 hours The greatest concern is across the exposed northern islands and eastern coastal areas Much of the Cagayan Valley especially west of the Sierra Madre Mountains should limited impacts WHERE IS THE STORM HEADING Forecast guidance continues to show two possible scenarios ECMWF and GFS A track closer to Taiwan potentially bringing destructive winds and flooding rainfall JTWC and Google DeepMind A sharper northward turn toward Ishigaki and Miyakojima in southern Japan The timing of an approaching trough will determine how quickly Champi turns north I currently favor a track closer to Ishigaki but there is still uncertainty Champi could maintain Category 4 or 5 equivalent intensity through Wednesday before gradually weakening as it approaches the southern Japanese islands later this week RAINFALL ACROSS THE PHILIPPINES While Champi moves well to the north its circulation continues to influence weather farther south Scattered showers and thunderstorms are expected across portions of Palawan Negros Iloilo Cebu and Mindanao through the remainder of the week and potentially into the weekend Meanwhile much of mainland Northern Luzon and Metro Manila should remain relatively dry apart from isolated showers as northeasterly winds become more established BOTTOM LINE Champi is a dangerous super typhoon but its most severe impacts are currently forecast for Taiwan or the southern Japanese islands not mainland Luzon Residents of Batanes Babuyan and exposed northeastern Luzon should still monitor PAGASA warnings closely A special thank you to Windy com for collaborating with text: TYPHOON KADIANG FLO STRUCK NORTHERN AND CENTRAL LUZON One of the most destructive and memorable weather events of the 1993 Pacific typhoon season On This Day OCTOBER 03 1993 Typhoon Kadiang PH International Name Flo made landfall between Isabela and Aurora coastline causing large storm surges At least 576 died and both an unknown number of missing and injured were reported from the typhoon In the capital Manila strong winds broke the moorings of a barge and another small freighter pushing them to the shorelines of the Roxas Boulevard The capital also experienced 93 mph winds from the storm Two more fishing ships MV Camiguan and MV Uniselva were also washed out in the shores off Manila Bay due to storm surges Mudflows from Mount Pinatubo were also triggered by the typhoon inundating houses in Pampanga Over 40,000 hectares of farmland were also destroyed and/or flooded in Central Luzon and Northern Luzon Widespread flooding were also reported at these areas including some parts of CALABARZON and Metro Manila Adding on over 384,802 families were affected As reported by the National Disaster Coordinating Council the total damages from the typhoon were estimated at PHP 5.3 billion 188 million 2005 USD The total deaths were finalized from 86 to 576 individuals making it one of the deadliest tropical cyclones to hit the country President Fidel V Ramos declared vast majority of Northern Luzon in state of calamity due to the catastrophic effects of FLO in the Philippines The president also approved 1.35 million for agricultural rehabilitation However these efforts were halted as Typhoon Husing PH IRA of early-November of the same season caused heavy destruction towards the country Philippine Weather Disturbances 03 October 2026 Kadiang1993 Typhoon Kadiang FLO1993 Typhoon FLO On This Day Throwback Tropical Cyclone Devastation

text: NCR-PRSD conducts training-workshop on flood forecasting and warning for Pampanga River Basin CITY OF SAN FERNANDO Pampanga The National Capital Region-PAGASA Regional Services Division NCR-PRSD through the Pampanga River Basin Flood Forecasting and Warning Center PRBFFWC conducted a training-workshop on Flood Forecasting and Warning System to strengthen flood forecasting warning operations and coordination among partner agencies in the Pampanga River Basin on October 13-16 2026 Held at the Social Action Center of Pampanga SACOP Ephata in Barangay Maimpis the activity focused on proving deeper understanding on river basin characteristics stream gaging flood forecasting and improving the clarity timeliness and dissemination of flood warnings to local government units and at-risk communities It also emphasized inter-agency coordination and the proper operation and maintenance of monitoring equipment to ensure reliable data for flood forecasting Participants discussed rainfall and river monitoring flood forecasting and procedures for issuing flood advisories and bulletins Sessions also covered how watershed characteristics influence flooding how floodwaters move through river systems and how post-flood assessments can inform future operations To complement the discussions participants conducted field exercises along the Pampanga River in San Luis Pampanga They surveyed the river's cross-section observed water levels measured flow velocity and calculated the volume of water flowing through the river-providing hands-on experience in collecting and interpreting data used in flood forecasting A workshop session titled From Warning to Action Partner Agencies Flood Response Protocol focused on coordinating agency responses to flood warnings Participants also shared feedback and recommendations on the center's flood advisories bulletins and visual presentation of information and identified opportunities for further collaboration Joining PRBFFWC personnel were representatives from the Office of Civil Defense-Region III Department of Science and Technology-Region III Mines and Geosciences Bureau-Region III National Irrigation Administration-Upper Pampanga River Integrated Irrigation Systems and the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices of Pampanga and Bulacan Participants from other agencies also expressed appreciation for the knowledge gained which are vital to support science-based decision-making process during extreme events affecting Pampanga River Basin NCRPRSD Pampanga River Basin text: MALUBHANG PAGBAHA SA DAVAO CITY BIBIGYANG SOLUSYON NI PANGULONG MARCOS USEC CASTRO Ibinahagi ni Palace Press Officer Atty Claire Castro na hindi magdadalawang isip si Pangulong Ferdinand Bongbong Marcos Jr na tulungan ang Davao City na maresolba ang umano'y malubhang pagbaha sa nasabing siyudad Sa isang press briefing nitong Agosto 27 2026 sinabi ni Castro na inatasan ng Pangulo si Department of Public Works and Highways DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon na tignan kung ano ang maaring gawing aksyon sa Davao City So lahat naman po ng lugar sa Pilipinas na binabaha ay tinutugunan ng ating pamahalaan at iyan po ang utos ng Pangulong Marcos Jr Kaya nga po noong sumobra ang baha sa Davao City hindi naman po nagpatumpik-tumpik ang Pangulo at si Secretary Vince Dizon na tulungan na ang Davao City dahil malubha na rin po ang pagbaha sa Davao ani Castro Maliban dito ay sinabi rin ni Castro ang kahalagahan ng mga dokumento upang malaman kung ano ba talaga ang naging progreso ng mga flood control project sa Davao City

text: LOOK Davao's La Verna Flood Control Basin Site C to Hold Almost 11 Olympic Pools of Rainwater Construction is moving forward at Site C of the three retarding basins rising along La Verna Creek in Buhangin part of the PHP 211 million flood control project of the Department of Public Works and Highways DPWH Davao City 3rd District Engineering Office Aerial footage taken on October 9 2026 shows excavators shaping the basin floor beside the existing La Verna pumping station along the Davao City Diversion Road CP Garcia Highway with boulders and steel sheet piles staged on site for the next phase of works Once completed Site C is designed to hold up to 27,260 cubic meters of stormwater or about 962,679 cubic feet That is almost 11 Olympic-size swimming pools worth of capacity from this site alone When all three sites are completed Sites A B and C will store a combined 79,460 cubic meters roughly equivalent to 32 Olympic-size swimming pools The basins will work hand in hand with the pumping station built in 2019 temporarily holding runoff during heavy rains and releasing it gradually toward the CAAP Outfall The goal is to end the street flooding that has long disrupted traffic in the La Verna area keeping one of Davao's busiest corridors safe and passable for thousands of daily commuters Metro Davao Rising Crown Jewel Of Mindanao Davao City Danny Betonio Raneses

text: DAVAO THE FLOOD CAPITAL BUT PERHAPS NOT FOR THE REASON YOU THINK They say Davao is the Flood Capital of the Philippines Well if someone insists on giving us that crown perhaps we should wear it proudly-but let's first ask a simple question What exactly is overflowing Yes Davao experiences floods We have rivers that swell after relentless rain low-lying communities that sometimes bear the brunt of nature sudden downpours that seem to arrive without an appointment and roads that occasionally transform into temporary swimming pools That is a real problem It deserves real solutions-not political theater But if we are going to compare cities perhaps the scoreboard deserves more than a political slogan During the severe southwest monsoon flooding in July 2025 for example the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority reported hundreds of flooding incidents across Metro Manila within a single day So before anyone points a finger at Davao perhaps we should remember that flooding is not a problem exclusive to one city Water does not check political affiliations before it rises Rain does not ask who you voted for before it pours And rivers certainly don't read campaign speeches But here's where I see Davao differently Because there is another kind of flooding happening here-one that doesn't destroy homes close roads or leave mud behind Davao floods with culture Walk through this city and you encounter a living mosaic of Mindanao Indigenous traditions migrant communities different languages cuisines beliefs stories and histories woven together into one constantly evolving urban tapestry Ask someone where they came from and you may discover an entire story behind the answer Then inevitably there's food Because in Davao you can start a conversation about almost anything and somehow end up discussing durian This variety is sweeter No that one has better texture You haven't tried the best one yet Suddenly what began as a casual conversation has transformed into an international conference on durian No registration fee required But perhaps Davao's most remarkable flood is neither water nor culture It is warmth There is a quiet generosity in the character of many Dabawenyos that statistics cannot measure You can arrive as a stranger and before long someone may already be telling you where to eat what places to visit which shortcut to take-and most importantly which road to avoid when traffic is terrible That's not just hospitality That's hospitality with a built-in traffic advisory And then there is Davao's natural beauty The sea Samal Mount Apo The forests The farms The rivers The mountains The wide spaces that remind you that progress and nature do not always have to be enemies Davao is also changing Businesses are arriving Buildings are rising Infrastructure is expanding Communities are growing People continue to come-not only because they are looking for jobs but because they are looking for possibilities Some arrive carrying résumés Others arrive carrying business plans Some arrive carrying nothing more than a dream And somewhere along the way many discover something unexpected They don't merely live in Davao They become part of it That perhaps is the real story A city should not be judged solely by the problems that rise within it It should also be judged by what its people continue to build despite those problems Davao is not perfect We have traffic We have growing pains We have environmental concerns We have infrastructure challenges We have political disagreements And of course we have social-media experts text: PHP 47 M Flood Control Project in Laoag Collapses Ties Emerge Between Contractor Linked to Davao Lawmaker and Sandro Marcos Office A newly built flood control structure along Padsan River in Barangay Gabu Laoag City a project worth PHP 47,024,704.34 funded under the 2024 General Appropriations Act GAA has collapsed JUST MONTHS after its reported completion sparking fresh outrage over the alleged flood-control mafia operating in Congress Photos taken on-site show large concrete revetments cracked dislodged and washed into the river exposing reinforcing steel and leaving the riverbank vulnerable to further erosion The project billboard names RA Pahati Construction and Supply Inc as the contractor under the DPWH Ilocos Norte First District Engineering Office with a target completion date of October 4 2024 RA Pahati Construction is reportedly owned by the family of Rep Jhong Ceniza of Pantukan Davao de Oro a name that has repeatedly surfaced in infrastructure procurement circles Sources familiar with congressional contracting allege that RA Pahati has become a favored builder for Rep Sandro Marcos the Ilocos Norte 1st District Representative allegedly with some help from his chief of staff said to be a relative of Rep Ceniza's wife Residents and local engineers have raised alarm over the collapse noting that the structure failed despite relatively moderate river flow in recent weeks Infrastructure experts point out that proper soil compaction adequate riprap foundation and correct steel reinforcement are crucial in river dike construction all of which appear deficient in the broken sections The collapse has revived long-circulating allegations about flood control allocations being used as a cash cow for certain districts RA Pahati controlled by the Ceniza family has reportedly bagged billions in contracts across Luzon and Mindanao despite originating from Davao de Oro In Ilocos Norte whispers persist that Rep Sandro Marcos chief of staff reportedly related by marriage to the Cenizas has been instrumental in channeling projects to RA Pahati bypassing stricter vetting Political analysts warn this could become a serious governance issue for the presidential son especially as calls mount for greater transparency in the use of massive DPWH flood control budgets The incident adds to the growing backlash against multi-billion flood control projects nationwide long suspected to be overpriced poorly built and politically manipulated In Congress several lawmakers particularly from Mindanao have been calling out selective investigations that spare politically allied districts while targeting rivals Observers warn that this Laoag project could become a flashpoint especially since it sits in the home turf of the President's son who is expected to champion good governance but now faces scrutiny over his district's infrastructure spending

text: STEADFAST SPIRIT Flash floods strike Davao City schools DepEd officials initiate Barog Leon AGSES to extend aid to severely affected school After catastrophic flooding left Leon A Garcia Sr Elementary School LAGSES with extensive damage to its classrooms learning materials and other school facilities the Department of Education DepEd Davao City Division officials launched the Barog Leon AGSES initiative mobilizing donations volunteers and community support to help restore the school and ensure learning continuity Located in Talomo East District Davao City Leon A Garcia Sr Elementary School is among the public schools repeatedly affected by flooding during periods of heavy rainfall with the recent floods blanketing the campus in thick mud and debris disrupting school operations and further highlighting the need for immediate rehabilitation efforts Barog Leon A Garcia Elementary School Ang bawat hamon na ating kinakaharap ay hindi hadlang upang muling makabangon Ang mahalaga ay patuloy tayong magtulungan magkaisa at maniwala na ang Leon A Garcia Sr Elementary School ay muling babangon nang mas matatag kaysa dati said Schools Division Superintendent Reynante A Solitario CESO V encouraging the school community to remain united and move forward despite the devastation caused by the floods Through the school's Lingap Kapwa Program donated supplies reached the most severely affected learners and families after an online survey and careful assessment helped ensure that assistance was directed to those who needed it most Recognizing that flooding is still a recurring challenge LAGSES remains steadfast to strengthen its disaster preparedness initiatives by promoting flood risk reduction enhancing emergency response systems ensuring learning continuity and advocating for safer more flood-resilient school facilities a shared commitment championed by the Department of Education to ensure that no learner is left behind even in times of crisis

and Coastal Defense Designed as a coastal bypass the project doubles as a breakwater and shore protection system defending against sea wave actions storm surges and coastal erosion It incorporates hexapods seawalls grouted riprap and other shoreline defenses to reduce wave impact-a thoughtfully engineered coastline safeguard 2 Integrated Roadway and Public Spaces The 4 lane highway with asphalt pavement bike lanes pedestrian sidewalks and a 25.54 meter full-width design serves mobility recreation and safety purposes Includes linear parks esplanades and promenades perfect for walking jogging or biking-offering both functional and leisure value 3 Strategic Flood Resilience The elevated embankmented structure approx 6.5 meters on average complete with drainage frameworks helps mitigate flooding from coastal surges and heavy rains Though technically it doesn't span rivers its design contributes indirectly to reducing flood impact in adjacent areas-especially during storm surges 4 Complementing River Flood Control Efforts Meanwhile along the Davao River DPWH is reinforcing revetment walls in Baranguay Mandug with structural sheet piles concrete capping and embankment fortification to control river flooding These efforts are nearing 90-94 percent completion and are slated for wrap-up by Q4 2025 These projects operate synergistically-coastal road handling storm surge while river revetment mitigates overflow inland 5 Timeline and Scale The 17.8 km coastal road also called the Coastal Bypass Road began in 2017 and is rolling out in phases with major segments already operational The iconic Bucana Bridge a 1.34 km P3.126 billion extradosed bridge linking coastal segments is under construction with completion expected by late 2025 Full project completion is targeted between 2025 to 2026 with approximately PHP 28.5 billion already utilized and more funding pending for final works tugpaagilaprojectupdates King City Of The South Philippines Crown Jewelof Mindanao Island

text: When the Waters Rise in Davao City So Do the Online Critics Following the heavy rains brought by the Habagat and recent weather systems on July 24 2026 several neighborhoods across Davao City once again faced rising floodwaters From Mandug and Tugbok down to low-lying areas like Bangkal Matina and Talomo families had to endure another stressful night of monitoring river levels moving to higher ground or waiting for emergency teams And like clockwork as soon as photos of flooded streets flooded social media the comments section lit up with the usual outrage political potshots and online bashing Where did the billions go Why hasn't the city solved flooding yet It is completely understandable for affected residents to feel frustrated when water enters their homes But using these calamities to mock or tear down the city overlooks the actual science geography and non-stop work happening on the ground Here is the perspective every Dabawenyo and onlooker needs to hear 1 You Cannot Out-Engineer a Catch Basin No politician regardless of their party and no amount of infrastructure spending can change basic topography Davao City sits beside major river systems Davao Talomo Matina Lipadas Bunawan and Lasang flowing straight into the gulf Key areas like Bago Gallera Talomo Proper Ulas Bangkal and Matina are natural catch basins When continuous rains hit the highlands upstream millions of gallons of water naturally rush downward into these lower elevations Add a high tide at the coast and the ocean acts like a giant dam preventing river mouths from discharging into the sea Dikes and pumping stations can help manage overflow but they cannot stop gravity or push back the ocean 2 Nature Remembers Its Original Shape Parts of Boulevard Bucana Agdao and Sta Ana were historically mudflats swamps and coastal wetlands Humans can pave over these landscapes with roads subdivisions and concrete structures but when extreme rainfall happens water simply reclaims its natural pathways With climate change intensifying weather patterns nationwide rainfall volumes that used to happen once every few decades are now occurring multiple times a year This is a regional and global environmental challenge not an isolated municipal flaw 3 Where Did the Funds Go Look at the Defense Systems in Place Critics often point to multi-billion flood control budgets as if money should make water instantly disappear But flood mitigation infrastructure isn't meant to stop rain from falling it's built to slow down water protect riverbanks and buy critical time Pumping Stations and Retarding Basins Built in notorious bottlenecks like Sasa and La Verna to hold runoff and force water past high-tide barriers Revetment Walls and Dikes Miles of concrete dikes line the Matina Talomo and Davao rivers to keep riverbanks from completely collapsing during sudden surges Early Warning and River Monitoring The City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office CDRRMO operates automated sensors and live HD monitoring cameras along all six major river channels allowing them to issue preemptive siren alarms and evacuation orders hours before water peaks 4 While Keyboard Warriors Bash Responders Are Out in the Dark While critics type away in dry rooms hundreds of frontline responders from the CDRRMO BFP Davao Light urban search and rescue SAR units and barangay disaster teams are out in waist-deep water executing rescue operations clearing clogged channels and moving stranded families to safety Good governance in a coastal river-dense city isn't measured by the complete absence of natural calamities it's measured by preparedness quick response and zero casualties The fact that emergency teams can track upstream river swells in real-time and mobilize rescue trucks within minutes is proof of a functional disaster system Bashing Davao City during a flood won't lower the tide and weaponizing human suffering for online arguments won't stop the rain Instead of tearing each other down let's focus on what actually keeps us safe community preparedness and cooperation When the CDRRMO issues a Code Red or sounds the warning siren do not wait Follow evacuation protocols early Look out for elderly neighbors keep your emergency kits ready and respect the responders risking their safety on the frontlines Davao City has faced heavy weather before and we will always stand resilient through it Stay safe stay vigilant and stay proud of our city Daghang salamat sa atong responders

text: WEATHER UPDATE Kalinga urged to prepare as Super Typhoon Champi Rosal approaches PAR Residents of Kalinga are advised to monitor weather updates and prepare for possible gusty winds and rain as Super Typhoon CHAMPI approaches the Philippine Area of Responsibility PAR according to the 11 p m tropical cyclone advisory issued by the Philippine Atmospheric Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration PAGASA on October 19 CHAMPI will be locally named ROSAL once it enters PAR was located 1,680 kilometers east of Southeastern Luzon as of 10 p m Monday It has maximum sustained winds of 195 kilometers per hour km/h gustiness of up to 240 km/h and is moving west northwestward at 15 km/h While Kalinga is not yet specifically identified in the advisory as an area expected to experience the strongest direct impacts the province may experience gusty conditions as the tropical cyclone moves closer to the country PAGASA said gusty conditions are likely to begin over most parts of Luzon and Visayas and portions of Mindanao by Wednesday October 21 Wind Signals may also be raised over the northern and eastern portions of Northern Luzon as early as Tuesday morning depending on the cyclone's development and forecast track The weather bureau also warned of possible heavy rainfall over Extreme Northern Luzon while moderate to rough seas may affect the northern and eastern seaboards of Luzon beginning Tuesday Hazardous sea conditions may develop from Wednesday onward CHAMPI is expected to maintain its super typhoon strength upon entering PAR with further intensification still possible over the Philippine Sea It is forecast to turn northward on Wednesday and begin weakening by Thursday October 22 Although the current advisory does not specify the exact rainfall and wind conditions expected in Kalinga residents are encouraged to remain alert particularly those living in landslide-prone and flood-prone areas Local disaster risk reduction and management offices are likewise advised to monitor succeeding PAGASA bulletins and prepare for possible weather-related incidents PAGASA is expected to issue its next tropical cyclone advisory at 11 a m on October 20 DOST PAGASA

text: LOOK Davao's La Verna Flood Control Basin Site C to Hold Almost 11 Olympic Pools of Rainwater Construction is moving forward at Site C of the three retarding basins rising along La Verna Creek in Buhangin part of the PHP 211 million flood control project of the Department of Public Works and Highways DPWH Davao City 3rd District Engineering Office Aerial footage taken on October 9 2026 shows excavators shaping the basin floor beside the existing La Verna pumping station along the Davao City Diversion Road CP Garcia Highway with boulders and steel sheet piles staged on site for the next phase of works Once completed Site C is designed to hold up to 27,260 cubic meters of stormwater or about 962,679 cubic feet That is almost 11 Olympic-size swimming pools worth of capacity from this site alone When all three sites are completed Sites A B and C will store a combined 79,460 cubic meters roughly equivalent to 32 Olympic-size swimming pools The basins will work hand in hand with the pumping station built in 2019 temporarily holding runoff during heavy rains and releasing it gradually toward the CAAP Outfall The goal is to end the street flooding that has long disrupted traffic in the La Verna area keeping one of Davao's busiest corridors safe and passable for thousands of daily commuters Metro Davao Rising Crown Jewel Of Mindanao Davao City Danny Betonio Raneses

text: ROBREDO EXPLAINS P500 M GRANT FOR JESSE ROBREDO COLISEUM Naga City Mayor Leni Robredo said she sought national government funding to rehabilitate the Jesse Robredo Coliseum which has increasingly served as the city's main evacuation center despite not being originally designed for that purpose Built in 2009 and opened in 2010 the 12,000 seat coliseum has housed thousands of families during disasters However it lacks adequate spaces for tents beds communal kitchens relief goods and flood-safe comfort rooms The need for rehabilitation became more urgent after Typhoon Kristine caused severe flooding in Naga Robredo said she sought funding upon assuming office in 2025 and was advised to apply for Local Government Support Fund LGSF assistance The request was approved with P450 million allocated for rehabilitation and P50 million for heavy equipment She added that construction is expected to begin in October 2026 after government and non-government offices currently housed at the coliseum are relocated to the Balatas Building Leni Robredo

text: HIGHER DIKE BUILT ALONG TALOMO RIVER IN DAVAO CITY A higher dike has been completed along a portion of the Talomo River in Davao City with the project finished within just two months after Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon ordered the immediate resumption and elevation of the river control structure The project was originally started in 2019 to help prevent severe flooding in communities located near the river The move followed President Ferdinand Marcos Jr s directive to raise the structure by two meters on both sides of the river to help address flooding in the area The planned elevation of the dike was reportedly not pursued at the time allowing the river to overflow and affect nearby homes Department of Public Works and Highways

text: Signal No 1 up in parts of Northern Luzon due to Rosal By Cristina Arayata MANILA Wind Signal No 1 has been hoisted in parts of Northern Luzon as Super Typhoon Rosal international name Champi entered the Philippine Area of Responsibility PAR at around 10:40 a m Tuesday Areas under Signal No 1 are Batanes eastern portion of Babuyan Islands Babuyan Is Camiguin Is Didicas Is eastern portion of mainland Cagayan Santa Ana Gonzaga Lal-Lo Santa Teresita Camalaniugan Aparri Buguey Gattaran Baggao Peñablanca northeastern portion of Isabela Maconacon Divilacan Palanan San Pablo Cabagan Santa Maria Tumauini Ilagan City and northeastern portion of Catanduanes Pandan Bagamanoc Panganiban Viga Gigmoto It doesn't mean that these areas will immediately feel the effects of the wind signal There are at least 36 hours for the people in these areas to prepare for the strong winds Philippine Atmospheric Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration PAGASA forecaster Chris Perez said in a press conference The cyclone was located 1,385 kilometers east of Central Luzon outside of PAR as of 10 a m It is moving west northwestward at 25 kilometers per hour kph Rosal packs maximum sustained winds of 185 kph near the center and gustiness of up to 230 kph It is not directly affecting any part of the country The cyclone is forecast to move towards extreme Northern Luzon Taiwan area in the coming days Perez said He said no significant rainfall is expected in the next 24 hours Perez however said that in the coming days the wind signal may be raised to No 2 or 3 as Rosal moves closer to Northern Luzon As of Tuesday PAGASA said the northeasterly windflow and Rosal's periphery will cause strong to gale-force gusts across Batanes Ilocos Norte Cagayan Isabela Polillo Islands Camarines Norte Camarines Sur Catanduanes Northern Samar Eastern Samar most of Caraga Camiguin Misamis Oriental Sarangani Davao del Sur and Davao Occidental Meanwhile the cyclone is forecast to weaken into a typhoon on Thursday It is expected to exit PAR on Saturday Perez added Disaster response Meanwhile the Office of Civil Defense OCD called on all authorities and the public to take the necessary measures to limit the impact of Rosal In an advisory late Monday the OCD urged regional and local disaster risk reduction and management councils to strengthen monitoring review contingency plans preposition response resources and ensure the readiness of personnel equipment evacuation centers and critical facilities It also urged closer monitoring of rainfall river and reservoir levels tides low-lying and landslide-prone areas coordinate early warnings and possible preemptive evacuations and prioritize vulnerable groups including persons with disabilities senior citizens and children The public is advised to monitor official weather bulletins and local government advisories prepare emergency supplies secure essential documents and be ready to evacuate when instructed Communities are reminded that the ongoing El Niño conditions do not eliminate the risks of sudden heavy rainfall flash floods landslides and other hazards it said thus the need for timely coordinated action and sustained public vigilance to protect lives and minimize the potential impacts of the weather disturbance The Philippine National Police has also alerted its field units and ordered the activation of disaster response measures in areas affected by Rosal With a reports from Priam Nepomuceno and Lloyd Caliwan/PNA Graphics from PAGASA

text: Disclaimer This article is intended for my Journalism class A Million to One by Kent Sanchez Millions suffer thousands die and only a few can ever get a taste of paradise Beneath every struggle of a Filipino with the frequent flooding there are those whose greed comes first before public service As the country struggles to cope with the aftermath of natural disasters Davao is no stranger to these occurrences Roads turn invisible dirty rainwater reaches knee-level and some end up in hospitals from diseases they never wished to become victims of 265 flood-prone areas were identified in Davao City by the City Engineer's Office CEO most of which were also distinguished to be in District 1 according to David Ezra M Francisquete of Sunstar Davao Due to these incidents Christian a Barangay Rafael Castillo Lanang resident recalled a past experience with flooding in the area He explained how Lanang is at risk of flooding incidents Lanang is considered a coastal area because it sits right along the Davao Gulf a body of water on the southeastern coast of Mindanao This means that when heavy rains coincide with high tide flooding is almost inevitable for homes near the shore He 16 2024 DUE TO HEAVY RAINS BROUGHT ABOUT BY THE SHEAR LINE AND NORTHEAST MONSOON WHEREAS since the early evening of January 15 2024 Davao City has been experiencing heavy rains continuing into the morning of January 16 2024 due to a shear line and localized thunderstorms affecting Mindanao WHEREAS at 4:11 AM of January 16 2024 the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council NDRRMC issued an Orange Rainfall Warning for Davao Oriental and Davao de Oro warning of possible heavy rains flash floods and landslides in said areas WHEREAS at 6:00 AM of January 16 2024 the Department of Science and Technology Philippine Atmospheric Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration DOST-PAGASA issued General Flood Advisory Number 2 for Region XI Davao Region which forecasts light to moderate rains and thunderstorms in the region for the next 12 hours due to the shear line affecting the northern and eastern sections of Mindanao and the northeast monsoon affecting Luzon and Visayas WHEREAS the City Government of Davao is duty-bound to safeguard the welfare of the public and undertake measures to avert any untoward incidents or disasters that may be caused by the effects of said weather occurrence NOW THEREFORE I SEBASTIAN Z DUTERTE Mayor of the City of Davao by virtue of the powers vested in me by law do hereby declare the following to take effect on Tuesday January 16 2024:1 That classes and school activities in ALL LEVELS in all public and private educational institutions in Davao City are hereby suspended 2 That the Work-From-Home WFH arrangement shall be adopted in all national and local government offices including government-owned and controlled corporations in Davao City EXCEPT for offices performing safety and security health social services and disaster and emergency response services and 3 That private offices and establishments are given the discretion to suspend work or adopt WFH arrangements but are encouraged to do so for the safety and convenience of their employees Done this 16th day of January 2024 in Davao City Philippines

text: DAVAO'S FLOOD MAP EXPLAINED Why Different Neighborhoods Face Different Flood Risks When heavy rains hit Davao City why do some neighborhoods experience sudden flash floods that recede in a few hours while others remain submerged under standing water for days It all comes down to catchment hydrology The master plan developed by the Department of Public Works and Highways DPWH and the Japan International Cooperation Agency JICA covers 2,200 square kilometers divided into three main river basins Because each catchment has a unique shape slope and size each one poses a completely different flood threat to specific Davao neighborhoods 1 Davao River Basin 1,755 km2 Massive Volume and Standing Water Neighborhoods Affected Waan Tigatto Ma-a Barangay 19 Barangay 8 and Bucana What Happens Here This is the largest river system in the area Because its catchment extends deep into the northern mountain ranges it collects enormous volumes of rainwater Even when it isn't raining in the downtown area heavy rainfall up in the mountains eventually travels downstream into the city The Engineering Reality Because the basin is so large there is a time delay before the main wave of water reaches the city As the river passes through tight natural bends near Tigatto and Ma-a the channel gets squeezed forcing water over the banks Worse when peak river flows meet high tides at the river mouth in Bucana the seawater acts like a natural dam This creates a severe backwater effect that traps floodwaters inland causing deep slow-draining pools that cover over 480 hectares and affect 43,000 residents 2 Matina River Basin 70 km2 Rapid Flash Floods and Highway Bottlenecks Neighborhoods Affected Matina Pangi Gravahan GSIS Subdivision and Matina Crossing What Happens Here Unlike the Davao River Matina suffers from sudden high-speed flash floods with very little warning time The Engineering Reality This basin is relatively small steep and heavily built-up with concrete and asphalt Because rainwater cannot soak into the ground it immediately rushes straight into the river channel Narrow bridge openings-such as the crossing along McArthur Highway-act like narrow bottlenecks When high-volume runoff reaches these tight spots the water backs up rapidly and spills sideways over the banks directly into nearby residential subdivisions 3 Talomo River Basin 204 km2 Raging Currents and Riverbank Collapse Neighborhoods Affected Talomo Proper Tugbok and communities along the Talomo Riverbanks What Happens Here While Talomo does not usually create broad standing lakes like the Davao River its waters move at extremely high speeds as they surge down from the slopes of Mount Apo The Engineering Reality The steep drop in elevation gives the rushing water tremendous kinetic energy Instead of long-term standing pools the main danger here is high-velocity water scraping against the riverbed and riverbanks This severe erosion tears away the surrounding land threatens bridge piers and causes steep riverbanks to collapse along the Talomo-Tugbok corridor 4 The Missing Gaps Intermediate Basins and Urban Creeks Neighborhoods Affected Toril Lipadas River Bunawan and Lasang Bunawan/Licanan Rivers and Agdao Bajada and Buhangin Urban Creek Networks The Planning Limitation On master plan maps you might notice uncolored spaces between the three big basins In nature land is continuous-every square meter belongs to a catchment The JICA study intentionally focused its scope on the three largest high-volume river mains omitting these smaller intermediate catchments Why They Still Matter These smaller watersheds carry severe flood risk For instance the Lipadas River in Toril causes rapid flash evacuations the Bunawan River frequently submerges portions of the Davao-Agusan Highway and dense urban creek networks in Agdao and Buhangin overflow quickly during short thunderstorms because over 95 percent of the city's natural urban wetlands have been paved over Comprehensive city drainage requires addressing these omitted gaps alongside the main rivers The Takeaway Whether it's standing water along the Davao River flash flooding in Matina riverbank erosion in Talomo or creek overflow in Agdao and Toril any effective flood strategy must treat all catchments as interconnected systems DAVAO FLOOD CONTROL SERIES 4 PART DEEP DIVE Read the Full Overview Post Here PART 1 text: LOOK The Department of Science and Technology XI DOST XI in partnership with HELP Davao Network Davao Central College DCC and the International Center for Water Hazard and Risk Management ICHARM Japan is conducting a hands-on training on the Davao Region Online Synthesis System DROSS to strengthen disaster resilience efforts in the region During the morning session Dr Anthony Sales DOST XI Regional Director emphasized the importance of science-driven solutions in mitigating flood risks Prof Toshio Koike of ICHARM Japan provided global perspectives on disaster resilience and the need for transformative steps towards sustainability DENR XI Regional Director represented by Dr Franklyn R Buenaflor reaffirmed its commitment to supporting scientific initiatives for disaster preparedness The training also featured discussions on flooding incidents in Davao Region scientific early warning systems and climate outlook for 2025 with experts from PAGASA CDRRMO and local hazard management teams presenting crucial data The hands-on session in the afternoon will equip participants with practical skills to utilize DROSS for disaster risk reduction This initiative strengthens regional efforts in flood forecasting early warning systems and climate adaptation strategies DOSTXI Disaster Resilience DROSS Science For The People DOST Davao One DOST4U ICHARM Japan

matapos ang pagbaha sa Davao City Pero bago gawing political weapon ang isang kalamidad baka kailangan muna nating maintindihan ang totoong nangyari EDUKASYON MUNA BAGO PANG-IINSULTO 1 SINO BA ANG NAGSABING HINDI BINABAHA ANG DAVAO CITY Walang lungsod sa mundo ang hindi binabaha Kahit ang mga highly developed cities tulad ng Singapore ay nakakaranas din ng pagbaha Ang pagiging maunlad ay hindi nangangahulugan na imposibleng tamaan ng kalamidad Ang Davao City ay hindi simpleng siyudad lamang Ito ang pinakamalaking lungsod sa Pilipinas ayon sa lawak ng lupain Halos 4 na beses ang lawak ng Metro Manila May malawak na kabundukan watershed areas ilog at mabababang lugar Hindi lahat ng baha ay pare-pareho 2 BAKIT BINABAHA ANG DAVAO KAHIT MINSAN WALANG MALAKAS NA ULAN SA DOWNTOWN Dahil ang Davao City ay bahagi ng malalaking river systems Kasama rito ang Lasang River Basin Bunawan River Basin Davao River Basin Matina River Basin Talomo River Basin Lipadas River Basin Sibulan River Basin Ang Davao River at mga tributaries nito tulad ng Panigan at Tamugan Rivers ay nagsisilbing daluyan ng tubig mula sa kabundukan pababa sa Davao Gulf Kaya kapag malakas ang ulan sa upland areas o kabundukan Bababa ang tubig Tataas ang water level ng mga ilog Maaapektuhan ang low-lying areas Ito ang tinatawag na upstream runoff Hindi lahat ng tubig ay galing sa mismong lugar na binaha 3 HINDI LANG DAVAO ANG BINAGYO NG KALAMIDAD Sa nakalipas na 48 oras 17 lungsod sa NCR ang naapektuhan ng baha 6 lungsod sa Region III 5 lungsod sa Region IV-A May mga naapektuhan din sa Region VI VII at XII At isang lungsod sa Davao Region ang Davao City Pero bakit parang Davao lamang ang pinag-uusapan Bakit ang sakuna ng isang lungsod ay ginagawang pagkakataon para mangutya 4 ANG BAHA AY HINDI TAGUMPAY NG KAHIT SINONG PANIG Masakit isipin na may ilang taong natuwa sa paghihirap ng iba May mga nagsasabing deserve ninyo yan Pero kailan naging tama ang pagsasaya sa kalamidad Ang baha ay hindi pumipili ng kulay ng politika Hindi nito tinatanong kung sino ang sinusuportahan mo Kapag may sakuna ang unang dapat lumabas ay malasakit hindi pangungutya 5 OO MAY KARAPATANG MAGTANONG ANG MGA DABAWENYO Hindi ibig sabihin na ipinagtatanggol ang Davao ay wala nang dapat ayusin May karapatan ang mga residente na humingi ng Mas mahusay na flood control Mas mabilis na disaster response Mas matibay na infrastructure Mas epektibong paghahanda Kung may pagkukulang ang pamahalaan dapat itong punahin Ang accountability ay bahagi ng demokrasya Pero ang pagpuna ay iba sa pang-iinsulto 6 ANG HINDI NAKIKITA NG IBA DAVAO KNOWS HOW TO RECOVER Totoo Nakakatakot ang flash floods Malakas ang agos May mga sasakyan at ari-arian na naaapektuhan Pero isang mahalagang katotohanan Ang tubig ay mabilis ding humuhupa Dahil sa natural na topograpiya at daluyan ng mga ilog matapos dumaan ang malaking volume ng tubig mula sa uplands mabilis na bumababa ang baha sa maraming lugar Hindi perpekto ang sistema Pero hindi rin tama na husgahan ang buong lungsod dahil lamang sa isang kalamidad 7 ANG DAVAO AY MAY SISTEMA NG PAGHAHANDA Bago pa lumala ang sitwasyon May early warning systems May monitoring ng water levels May rescue operations May preemptive evacuations Bukas agad ang mga health centers para sa wound care at leptospirosis prevention Hindi hinihintay ng mga responder na maging huli ang lahat bago kumilos Sa huli Maaari tayong magkaiba ng opinyon sa politika Maaari tayong pumuna Maaari tayong humingi ng pagbabago Pero sana huwag nating mawala ang pinakamahalagang bagay Ang pagiging tao Ang baha ay hindi dahilan para mawala ang respeto at malasakit sa kapwa Pilipino Davao will recover Hindi dahil perpekto ang lungsod Kundi dahil ang mga Dabawenyo ay sanay humarap sa unos tumulong text: Barangay sent 3 warning letters before Callawa Bridge 2 collapse PACC says DAVAO CITY The Presidential Anti-Corruption Commission PACC has launched a formal investigation into the collapse of Callawa Bridge 2 after learning that the Barangay Council of Callawa had allegedly sent at least three warning letters to the Department of Public Works and Highways DPWH before the structure gave way last week According to the PACC the letters raised serious concerns over visible cracks on the bridge severe erosion beneath the structure exposed bridge foundations and posts and the possibility that the bridge could collapse during heavy flooding Residents and barangay officials claimed the warnings were repeatedly brought to the attention of authorities but were allegedly never properly acted upon The bridge collapsed on May 18 following continuous heavy rains triggered by the Intertropical Convergence Zone ITCZ and Easterlies disrupting transportation access and affecting residents and motorists in Barangay Callawa and nearby communities During an ocular inspection conducted Friday PACC officials and volunteer engineers observed extensive erosion and scouring along the bridge approaches with large portions of supporting soil already washed away by strong floodwaters PACC Chairman Dr Louie F Ceniza said the incident raises serious concerns about accountability and public safety If prior warnings were indeed raised by the Barangay Council and residents these concerns should have been immediately addressed before the situation escalated into a disaster Ceniza said The people deserve answers The public deserves accountability he added The inspection was conducted in the presence of PACC BOT Member Rev Richie Cubos DPWH Davao City 3rd District Engineering Office Assistant District Engineer Andrew Pangan and volunteer civil engineers from Davao City assisting in the initial technical assessment The collapsed structure forms part of the DPWH Region XI infrastructure project identified as Project ID No 17L00133 covering the concreting widening and improvement of the Buhangin-Tigatto-Mandug-Callawa-Fatima Road including reconstruction of Callawa Bridge The project implemented by DPWH Region XI and undertaken by contractor Premium Megastructures Inc cost P190.7 million and was completed in December 2018 Initial observations by the PACC indicated that the bridge may have lacked sufficient upstream and downstream flood protection measures Investigators said approximately 100 meters of flood control protection on both sides of the bridge could have minimized or prevented the erosion that undermined the structure The PACC also noted the collapse of nearby utility poles due to severe soil erosion and loss of support As part of the probe the commission said it will review approved engineering plans hydraulic and geotechnical studies construction quality control reports inspection and acceptance records maintenance documents and all correspondence submitted by Barangay Callawa including DPWH responses to the reported concerns PACC BOT Member and Spiritual Adviser Bishop Rod Cubos said the incident highlights the text: THE HOSTAGE BLUEPRINT JICA MASTERPLAN FOR DAVAO CITY What if I told you that a blueprint to stop the flooding in Davao City is already finished It was designed by some of the best engineers in the world printed and is currently sitting on a desk in Manila Here is the truth about the JICA Master Plan the political war currently holding it hostage and what our Local Government Unit LGU is doing to keep our heads above water while we wait The Real Solution The JICA Master Plan Back in 2018 the Philippine government partnered with the Japan International Cooperation Agency JICA to solve our city's flooding Instead of just building basic concrete walls which easily overflow the Japanese and local engineers designed a massive city-wide system The core of the plan involves digging massive retarding basins giant empty catch-ponds built in the uplands When a storm hits millions of gallons of water would flow into these basins and be held there safely trapping the water before it ever reaches barangays like Ma-a Matina and Talomo It is brilliant it is proven and it is ready But just look at the timeline of how it got stuck in politics Here is the timeline April 2019 THE STUDY BEGINS The Philippine government and the Japan International Cooperation Agency JICA sign an agreement to create a long-term multi-basin master plan 2018-2022 WHY WASN'T IT BUILT UNDER DUTERTE A common question is why this wasn't funded during former President Rodrigo Duterte's term The answer is engineering reality The Japanese engineers were still studying our rivers You cannot fund or construct a mega-project when the architects haven't finished the blueprints July 2023 THE BLUEPRINT IS FINISHED JICA officially completes the Master Plan Instead of basic walls it proposes PHP 41.7 Billion to build massive retarding basins giant empty bowls upstream to catch and hold storm water before it hits our urban barangays AUGUST 9 2024 VP SARA CALLS OUT THE MISSING BUDGET Vice President Sara Duterte issues a strong public statement pointing out the lack of government action She calls out the current administration for refusing to fund the finalized master plan questioning if the budget is being intentionally withheld simply because the sitting mayor is a Duterte Baka naman may alinlangan pa hinggil dito dahil Duterte ang mayor at mas mamarapatin nilang gibain na lang she stated 2025 Present STILL WAITING FOR FUNDS Despite the blueprint being ready for over two years the national government has still not released the funding needed to actually build it Bureaucracy or Sabotage While politicians debate whether the delay is just standard government red tape for a foreign loan or a deliberate political attack to damage the Duterte family ordinary Davaoeños are the collateral damage We are the ones sweeping mud out of our homes The ultimate solution to our flooding is being treated as a political football What is the LGU Doing While We Wait The Davao City local government cannot afford a PHP 41.7 Billion mega-project on its own They cannot single-handedly buy multi-hectare lands to build giant retarding ponds without national funding However they are not just sitting around waiting for our government Without the big blueprint the LGU is focusing heavily on immediate urban drainage nature-based mitigation and survival Here is what the city is doing right now Aggressive Drainage and Inlet Upgrades The City Engineer's Office CEO and Task Force Drainage are continuously ripping up flood-prone choke points In 2025 alone they funded five new major inlet projects to help water subside faster on critical roads like Diversion Road fronting Panacan Cemetery Quezon Boulevard and Cabantian-Bunawan Preventing Blockages The city's Ancillary Services Unit ASU is conducting aggressive year-round desilting and garbage clearing of these new drainage systems so the street-level water actually has somewhere to go Smart Early Warning Systems If the LGU cannot completely stop the water they focus on keeping people alive Davao City relies heavily on its high-definition river cameras monitoring the Talomo Matina and Davao rivers 24/7 This real-time data triggers sirens and preemptive evacuations long before the flood hits living rooms Wetlands Protection The city is pushing for stricter zoning laws to protect remaining natural wetlands and ponding areas from being paved over by commercial developers allowing nature to absorb some of the rainwater According to local environmental groups like the Interface Development Intervention for Sustainability IDIS Davao City has lost a staggering 95 percent of its natural wetlands since 1945 due to rapid unchecked urban development Many of today's worst flood zones used to be natural swamps and marshes that absorbed rainwater As an alternative to concrete dams the LGU can focus on Nature-based Solutions NbS This includes legally protecting

text: P1.4 B DPWH contracts tied to Rep Ceniza's construction firm P1.4 B DPWH Contracts Tied to Rep Ceniza's Construction Firm A construction company linked to Davao de Oro 2nd District Rep Jhong Ceniza has secured at least PHP 1.41 billion worth of flood control projects from the Department of Public Works and Highways DPWH between 2022 and 2025 Documents from the Securities and Exchange Commission identify R A Pahati Construction and Supply Inc as a contractor where Ceniza-whose full name is Leonel Domo-ong Ceniza-and his wife Jella Pahati Ceniza are listed as incorporators Among its projects were the PHP 35 million Mabo Creek revetment leading to the Kingking River and the PHP 95 million Matilao River revetment both awarded in 2023 while Ceniza was still mayor of Pantukan Davao de Oro The timing has drawn scrutiny over potential conflicts of interest The company also implemented the PHP 150 million Davao River revetment rehabilitation in Barangay Mandug Davao City in 2024 as well as the PHP 86.8 million Saug River flood control project in Asuncion Davao del Norte in 2022 Outside Mindanao R A Pahati obtained 13 projects worth PHP 633 million in Nueva Ecija two projects worth PHP 145 million in Zambales and a PHP 72.3 million contract in Pampanga Additional projects were awarded in Bulacan Ilocos Norte Camarines Sur and Laguna Sen Rodante Marcoleta earlier flagged the firm among contractors that benefited from more than a billion pesos in DPWH-funded flood control projects warning that some of these may be ghost projects Ceniza dismissed the allegations as recycled political attacks These are old issues that were hurled at me during the last elections he said stressing that he had been in the construction business before entering politics I was never involved in any ghost projects If my name surfaced it was not because of any anomaly as my opponents want to portray he added expressing confidence that his family's reputation will be cleared Despite cornering PHP 1.41 billion in contracts R A Pahati Construction did not appear on the DPWH's list of the top 15 contractors with the biggest flood control project allocations Front Page everyoneシ゚ text: PANGULONG MARCOS IPINAG-UTOS NA BIGYANG SOLUSYON ANG MALALANG PAGBAHA SA DAVAO CITY USEC CASTRO Ipinag-utos ni Pangulong Ferdinand Bongbong Marcos Jr na bigyang solusyon ang umano'y malalang pagbaha sa Davao City ayon kay Palace Press Officer Atty Claire Castro Sa isang press briefing nitong Agosto 26 2026 sinabi ni Castro na iniutos ni Marcos Jr kay Department of Public Works and Highways DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon na ipatupad ang mga proyekto na makakabawas sa pagbaha sa nasabing siyudad na balwarte ng mga Duterte Ayon kay Castro ay nakita umano ng gobyerno na sampung taon na walang nangyaring dredging sa Davao City Nagpabigay na agad ng utos ang Pangulo kay Secretary Vince Dizon na ayusin ang pagbabaha malalang pagbabaha sa Davao City At nakita po ni Secretary Vince Dizon na mayroong isang proyekto doon na 2019 pa ay hindi naaayos ani Castro At sa sampung taon ay walang dredging na ginawa Kaya po inutos ng Pangulo agad-agad itong ayusin para sa mga kababayan natin sa Davao City dagdag pa niya Samantala ay sinabi rin ni Castro na kailangang silipin kung totoo nga bang nakumpleto ang 13,970 na flood control projects noong panahon ni dating Pangulong Rodrigo Duterte

text: CASTRO PBBM BINANTAYAN PA RIN ANG HABAGAT HABANG NASA BIRTHDAY NI FL LIZA Dinepensahan ng Malacañang si Pangulong Ferdinand Bongbong Marcos Jr matapos kumalat online ang mga video ng kanyang pagkanta sa birthday celebration ni First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos habang nakararanas ng malalakas na pag-ulan at pagbaha ang ilang bahagi ng bansa Ayon kay Palace Press Officer Claire Castro hindi umano tumigil sa pagtupad ng kanyang tungkulin ang Pangulo kahit naglaan ito ng oras upang makasama ang kanyang pamilya sa ika 67 kaarawan ng First Lady Ang Pangulo ay Pangulo saan man siya naroroon Ang paglalaan ng ilang oras para sa kanyang pamilya ay hindi nangangahulugang tumitigil ang kanyang tungkulin o ang operasyon ng pamahalaan ani Castro Dagdag niya patuloy umanong minomonitor ni Marcos ang epekto ng pinalakas na southwest monsoon o habagat at nagbigay ng direktiba sa mga kinauukulang ahensya upang agad na tumugon sa mga apektadong lugar Sa gitna ng matinding pag-ulan patuloy ang kanyang pagbabantay at pag-uutos sa mga ahensya upang matiyak ang kaligtasan at agarang pagtulong sa ating mga kababayan dagdag ni Castro Nauna nang naging viral ang mga video ng Pangulo habang kumakanta para sa kanyang asawa sa birthday celebration nito Kasabay nito ilang lugar sa Luzon ang nakaranas ng matinding pag-ulan at pagbaha dahil sa habagat

text: LAHAT NG KURAP I-FIRING SQUAD VILLANUEVA NANAWAGAN NG MATINDING PARUSA SA NASA LIKOD NG FLOOD-CONTROL ANOMALY Ito ang matapang na mungkahi ni Senator Joel Villanueva para sa mga taong aniya'y dapat managot sa umano'y mga anomalya sa flood-control projects habang patuloy na nararanasan ng ilang komunidad sa Bulacan ang pagbaha at pagguho ng lupa Sa pagdinig ng Senado kaugnay ng panukalang 2027 budget ng Commission on Audit COA mariing nagpahayag si Villanueva ng kanyang pagkadismaya sa mga responsable umano sa mga problemang may kinalaman sa flood-control projects OK ako sa firing squad sa mga yan Binigkas ito ng senador habang tinatalakay ang kalagayan ng ilang komunidad sa Bulacan na patuloy na nahaharap sa matinding pagbaha landslide at coastal erosion Ayon kay Villanueva may ilang barangay umano sa Bulacan na nanganganib nang tuluyang mawala dahil sa patuloy na pagguho ng lupa sa mga lugar na malapit sa baybayin Iginiit ng senador na kailangang mapanagot ang mga responsable sa anumang anomalya sa mga proyektong dapat sana ay nagpoprotekta sa mga komunidad laban sa pagbaha at iba pang sakuna Ang pahayag ni Villanueva ay kasunod ng paglilinaw ng COA na walang kinalamang ang senador sa mhga naging alegasyon ng maanumalyang flood control project

text: SINUNDAN NG PAGBAHA AT LANDSLIDE ANG KALBARYO NG MGA TAGA-SARANGANI SARANGANI PROVINCE Dagdag na pagsubok ang kinakaharap ngayon ng mga residente ng Sarangani matapos masundan ng malawakang pagbaha at mga pagguho ng lupa ang pinsalang iniwan ng tumamang 7.8 magnitude na lindol sa lalawigan Batay sa ulat rumagasa ang baha at nagkaroon ng mga landslide sa Barangay Lumasal Bayan ng Maasim na nagdulot ng matinding pinsala sa mga kalsada at tulay sa lugar Dahil dito nahirapan ang pagbiyahe ng mga motorista na papunta at pabalik ng General Santos City Patuloy ring nagbabala ang mga awtoridad sa posibleng karagdagang pagguho ng lupa lalo na sa mga lugar na nagkaroon na ng bitak at landslide bunsod ng naunang lindol Ayon sa mga obserbasyon maaaring humina na ang pundasyon ng mga apektadong bahagi ng kabundukan at lupa na lalong naging delikado dahil sa walang tigil na pag-ulan Nanawagan naman ang mga lokal na opisyal sa publiko na manatiling alerto at sundin ang mga abiso ng mga kinauukulang ahensya upang maiwasan ang anumang sakuna Samantala patuloy ang pagtatasa ng mga awtoridad sa lawak ng pinsala habang nagsasagawa rin ng mga hakbang upang matiyak ang kaligtasan ng mga residente at biyahero sa mga apektadong lugar Sarangani Pagbaha Landslide Maasim BANAT News Publishing

text: Meet the Surigao del Sur Meteorologist Who's Now with DOST-PAGASA Blaise Christian Perez 24 from Tandag City Surigao del Sur is the first graduate of a Bachelor of Science in Meteorology in the province turning his dream into reality The Surigaonon meteorologist studied at Bicol University and graduated in 2025 He now works in the Central Office of DOST-PAGASA Blaise shared with Ato Ni Bai that it took him multiple routes before landing in BS Meteorology BS Meteorology wasn't the most conventional choice and I was very aware of that when I decided to pursue it he said He applied to several universities including Adamson University and University of Southeastern Philippines for a different course but could not pursue it due to the pandemic He enrolled in BS Medical Laboratory Sciences at San Pedro College in Davao but it didn't work for him Blaise admitted that he wasn't fulfilled and struggled to stay motivated He applied again to another school but it did not work out Despite these setbacks he never lost sight of his childhood dream and chose to pursue it From a young age he was fascinated by how weather worked drawing inspiration from educational channels and science books especially about natural disasters His grandmother's encouragement of his interest in science nurtured this curiosity which later guided him back to his original dream despite exploring other paths There was this persistent feeling an instinct I couldn't ignore that I should go back to what I originally wanted So I applied for BS Meteorology at Bicol University which had always been my first choice he recalled According to Blaise meteorology was not just a chosen course it was his return to something that had always been part of him What began as a child's quiet curiosity about rain became a lifelong pursuit of understanding the atmosphere and more importantly using that understanding to serve and protect communities he said Now the Tandaganon meteorologist is working under the Hydrometeorology Division at the Central Office of DOST-PAGASA I'm working as a Project Technical Specialist under AI4RP at DOST-PAGASA primarily as a researcher within the agency So far the experience has been really fulfilling he shared From what once started as curiosity I now get to work on projects that combine meteorology research and even emerging technologies like AI for disaster risk reduction Beyond his research he was able to apply his expertise directly to help his community understand and respond to extreme weather events He proudly shared that he was given an opportunity to speak about the weather in the local language during coordination meetings with the Tandag CDRRMO for Bagyong Tino and Basyang These opportunities reinforced his commitment to giving back to his home province He feels a strong desire to contribute and work back in Surigao del Sur bringing what he has learned to help empower communities I really see the need to strengthen our local DRRM efforts especially in terms of climate resilience and more importantly effective science communication sa atong early warning systems Kitang tanan naka-experience kung unsa ka grabe ang epekto sa mga bagyo especially recently with TS Basyang nga nagdala og grabe nga pagbaha sa atoang probinsya labi na sa Tandag he said He also highlights that education and awareness are crucial and preparedness should be prioritized especially in the community People should be well-informed of PAGASA forecasts including warnings and know what to do before during and after a hazard Hindi man natin mapipigilan ang bagyo o ulan But through preparedness we can save lives ma minusan ang damage and make our communities more resilient he added To those planning to pursue meteorology Blaise shared that they should build a strong foundation in math and physics He advised them to stay curious and explore be patient with themselves and remember that the field is not just about forecasting it is about serving people and communities Padayon lang gyud even if the path feels uncertain or uncommon Dili man siya popular nga course but that doesn't make it any less important if anything mas kinahanglan pa gani siya karon he shared From a curious child in Tandag City to a meteorologist with plans for his home province's disaster preparedness Blaise shows how passion persistence and dedication can
